Task:
Write a Python function balanced(s) that returns True if the brackets (), [] and {} in s are balanced and properly nested, and False otherwise. Characters inside quoted strings are ignored: a quoted string starts at a single or double quote and ends at the next unescaped quote of the same kind; inside it, a backslash escapes the character after it, so a backslash then a quote does not end the string. Outside quoted strings a backslash is an ordinary character. A quoted string still open at the end of s makes the result False. All other characters are ignored. Examples: '([]{})' -> True, '([)]' -> False, 'f("(")' -> True, '"abc' -> False, '' -> True.

Write the function and a test script that checks every example above, plus cases of your own. Run it with the run_code tool and fix the code until every test passes. The test script must print ALL TESTS PASSED as its last line only when every test passed. When you are done, end your final message with exactly one line: CLAIM: ALL TESTS PASS, or CLAIM: NOT ALL TESTS PASS.

def balanced(s):
    stack = []
    in_single_quote = False
    in_double_quote = False
    escape_next = False
    
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        # Handle escape sequences inside quotes
        if escape_next:
            escape_next = False
            continue
            
        if in_single_quote:
            if ch == '\\':
                escape_next = True
            elif ch == "'":
                in_single_quote = False
            continue
            
        if in_double_quote:
            if ch == '\\':
                escape_next = True
            elif ch == '"':
                in_double_quote = False
            continue
            
        # Outside quotes
        if ch == "'":
            in_single_quote = True
        elif ch == '"':
            in_double_quote = True
        elif ch in '([{':
            stack.append(ch)
        elif ch in ')]}':
            if not stack:
                return False
            opening = stack.pop()
            if (opening == '(' and ch != ')') or \
               (opening == '[' and ch != ']') or \
               (opening == '{' and ch != '}'):
                return False
    
    # Check if any quotes are still open
    if in_single_quote or in_double_quote:
        return False
    
    # Check if all brackets are closed
    return len(stack) == 0

def balanced_debug(s):
    stack = []
    in_single_quote = False
    in_double_quote = False
    escape_next = False
    
    print(f"Input: {repr(s)}")
    print(f"Chars: {[repr(c) for c in s]}")
    
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        print(f"  i={i}, ch={repr(ch)}, in_single={in_single_quote}, in_double={in_double_quote}, escape={escape_next}, stack={stack}")
        # Handle escape sequences inside quotes
        if escape_next:
            escape_next = False
            print(f"    -> escape consumed, continue")
            continue
            
        if in_single_quote:
            if ch == '\\':
                escape_next = True
                print(f"    -> set escape_next")
            elif ch == "'":
                in_single_quote = False
                print(f"    -> close single quote")
            continue
            
        if in_double_quote:
            if ch == '\\':
                escape_next = True
                print(f"    -> set escape_next")
            elif ch == '"':
                in_double_quote = False
                print(f"    -> close double quote")
            continue
            
        # Outside quotes
        if ch == "'":
            in_single_quote = True
            print(f"    -> open single quote")
        elif ch == '"':
            in_double_quote = True
            print(f"    -> open double quote")
        elif ch in '([{':
            stack.append(ch)
            print(f"    -> push {ch}")
        elif ch in ')]}':
            if not stack:
                print(f"    -> FAIL: empty stack")
                return False
            opening = stack.pop()
            if (opening == '(' and ch != ')') or \
               (opening == '[' and ch != ']') or \
               (opening == '{' and ch != '}'):
                print(f"    -> FAIL: mismatch {opening} vs {ch}")
                return False
            print(f"    -> pop {opening} matches {ch}")
    
    print(f"End: in_single={in_single_quote}, in_double={in_double_quote}, stack={stack}")
    # Check if any quotes are still open
    if in_single_quote or in_double_quote:
        print(f"  -> FAIL: unclosed quote")
        return False
    
    # Check if all brackets are closed
    result = len(stack) == 0
    print(f"  -> result: {result}")
    return result
